description: Active deals. The spine of forecasting. Generic shape; map to your CRM in crm-profile/field-map.json.
corrections_note: Keys where the new definition must win over what a folder already holds, because the old value was a template defect rather than a choice someone made. contacts_engaged shipped as owner `local` and nothing ever wrote it, which is why single-threaded never fired. It is `derived` now and has to become derived in existing folders too, or the fix reaches nobody who already has one.

columns.name: forecast_category
columns.note: Some CRMs store a display name and an API value that differ (e.g. Commit stored as 'Forecast'). The profile records the mapping.

columns.name: amount
columns.note: The org's authoritative deal value. Which CRM field that is can be ambiguous — the profile names it.

columns.name: secondary_owner
columns.note: Co-owner or SE, where the org tracks one

columns.name: partner_id
columns.note: PARTNER- id when a partner is involved

columns.name: partner_role
columns.note: Sell-through = partner transacts. Sell-with = joint pursuit, we transact. They forecast differently and must not be summed together.

columns.name: deal_registration_id
columns.note: Partner deal registration reference, where the org uses one

columns.name: contacts_attached
columns.note: DERIVED rollup of opportunity-contacts.csv: how many people are on this deal at all, from the CRM's contact roles and from the activity record together. Free to compute and close to worthless as a risk signal on its own — being on a contact-role list says nothing about whether someone picks up the phone. It earns its place beside contacts_engaged, because the gap between the two is the interesting number.

columns.name: contacts_engaged
columns.note: DERIVED rollup of opportunity-contacts.csv: how many people have actually replied. This is the one the single-threaded flag reads. Blank, not zero, when the contacts registry is empty or the org's activity logging cannot establish direction — an absent answer that looks like a real one is the failure this column exists to avoid.

columns.name: close_plan_gaps
columns.note: DERIVED. Which close-plan elements are blank, semicolon-separated. This is the useful output, not the raw fields.

columns.name: risk_flags
columns.note: DERIVED, semicolon-separated: single-threaded;no-close-plan;date-slipped;stalled;no-champion. Four more come from opportunity-contacts.csv wherever it is populated — single-threaded;no-reply-ever;ghost-roles;auto-reply-only. Those are relationship risk and belong here, not in close_plan_gaps, which is hygiene.

columns.name: close_date_pushes
columns.note: How many times close date has moved out. The single best predictor of a deal that won't close.

columns.name: engagement_score
columns.note: DERIVED 0-100 from meetings, emails both ways, and notes in the recent window. Volume alone is weak — a deal with daily internal emails and no customer reply is not engaged.

columns.name: engagement_trend
columns.note: DERIVED by comparing the recent window against the one before it. DIRECTION, not level — a big deal ticking over steadily is not the same as a small one accelerating.

columns.name: meetings_recent
columns.note: DERIVED: meetings held in the current window

columns.name: emails_in_recent
columns.note: DERIVED: replies FROM the customer. The strongest single engagement signal — outbound volume measures effort, inbound measures interest.

columns.name: last_inbound_date
columns.note: DERIVED: last time they contacted us

columns.name: crm_last_modified
columns.note: The CRM's own last-modified stamp as at the last sync. Drift detection compares it against the CRM's current value; without it, which side changed a field is a guess.

columns.name: last_synced
columns.note: When this row was last reconciled against the CRM. A last_updated later than this means the row is ahead of the CRM and owes a push.
